sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:
It is the case of the petitioners that, on 04.06.2023 at about 3.05 to 3.10 p.m., when the deceased Latha M. @ Muthukrishnan Latha was proceeding in a scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KD-4476 as pillion driver on Sheshadri Road, near Anandrao Flyover down ramp, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-0932 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased motor cycle.
As a result of impact the deceased fell down on the right side and the rear wheel of the bus ran over the deceased due to which she sustained grievous injuries all over her body.

Immediately after the accident she was shifted to Victoria Hospital at Bengaluru,
wherein after examination doctors declared as brought dead.
Thereafter, Post mortem was conducted and the corpse was handed over to the family members.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards Medical Expenses, Conveyance, Death Ceremony, Obsequies and etc.

It is further urged that prior to the accident, deceased Latha M. @ Muthukrishnan Latha was hale and healthy and working as Assistant Accounts Officer and drawing salary of Rs.1,81,590/- per month and because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus and respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. After service of notice, the respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It is contended that the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary parties since for the alleged accident the rider of the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KD-4476 was solely responsible,
consequently the owner and insurer of the same are necessary parties.
The respondent has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

It has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KD-4476 in the accident and contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.
The respondent has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :

The petitioner No.1 is stated to be the husband, petitioner No.2 stated to be the daughter of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 has filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Adhaar cards marked at Ex.P13 and 14 do fortify the said fact.
Hence this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 and 2 are the legal heirs/representatives and dependents of deceased Latha M.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE NO.2 and 4:

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 04.06.2023 at about 3.05 to 3.10 p.m.,
when the deceased was proceeding as pillion rider in a scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KD-4476 on Anantharamakrishnan M.C vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37043003/
3 Sheshadri Road, near Anandrao Flyover down ramp, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-0932 came from behind right side at very high speed and dashed against the scooter in which deceased was proceeding, due to which she succumbed to the injuries and as such the respondent is liable to pay compensation to them.
10.

In order to substantiate the contentions, petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot mahazar,
Sketch, IMV Report, 133 notice and reply, Inquest Report, P.M. Report and Charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 10.

On the other hand, respondent has examined its driver as Rw.1 and he got marked the acknowledgment issued by the Upparpet Traffic Police station at Ex.R1.
11.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Bus.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

12. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Anandrao Flyover down ramp, Bengaluru, when the deceased person was proceeding in a Scooter as a pillion rider, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 0932 came with high speed in a rash and negligent Anantharamakrishnan M.C vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37043003/
4 manner and dashed to the deceased's two wheeler and caused the accident.

On the other hand Respondent contention is that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the scooter,
he came from service road and hit to the left side of the bus.

Even the driver of the bus also tried to lodge a complaint but police have not received the same and to prove this contention respondent's bus driver examined as Rw1 and relied on Ex.R1 which is the copy of complaint.
It was given on 19.06.2023 after 16 days of the accident and not explained the delay.

RW1 in his cross examination stated that he has given complaint on the day of accident but police have not taken, then he sent the complaint through post, then police gave endorsement, but he has not produced any postal receipt to show on the date of accident he has sent the complaint through post and also he has neither challenged the FIR and also Charge sheet before appropriate authority nor filed private complaint,
any prudent man cannot sit silently without taken any action if he has no fault in the accident.
But the driver of the Bus has not taken any legal action.
13. It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 and 4 which are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P4 it reflects that deceased was proceeding towards K.R Circle on Sheshardi road as a pillion rider in the two wheeler and suddenly the offending KSRTC bus came in a negligent manner and hit deceased's Scooter on the right side rear end, due to the impact pillion rider fell down on the road and the rear wheel of the bus ran over the deceased.
If the driver of bus had come in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicles who were playing on the road, then he could certainly avoid the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P5 IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more even the chargesheet as per Ex.P10 was also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P10 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the bus.

14. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

Even in the instant case though the driver of the bus is examined as RW.1 to show that there was no negligence on his part, even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.
15. The petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P10 clearly demonstrated that there was negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-F-0932 by its driver.

In view of discussion made supra, the negligence is attributed on the driver of the bus and hence question of joinder of owner and insurer of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KD-4476 as necessary parties does not arise at all.
Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.4 in the Negative.

Issue No.3:
16.

While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that the death of Latha M. @
Muthukrishnan Latha, was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0932.
17.
It is stated that the deceased was aged 55 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P15 which shows the date of birth as 06.02.1968.
The accident was occurred on 04.06.2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 55 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '11'.
18.

It is contended by the petitioners that, the deceased was working as Assistant Accounts Officer and drawing salary of Rs.1,81,590/- per month and she used to contribute entire income for the family maintenance.

In order to prove that deceased was working at Office of the Accountant General (A & E), Karnataka, her income and was an income tax assessee, petitioners have produced Ex.P11 and 12, Ex.P17 to P22 which are pay slips, IT returns, Form No.16 and ID Card.

19.
On perusal of the salary of the deceased for month of May-2023 as per Ex.P.30 was Rs.1,81,590/- and the same is taken into consideration as her monthly salary.
The annual income works out to Rs.21,79,080/- (1,81,590 X 12).

Out of the said annual income, professional tax &
income tax needs to be deducted.

In the case on hand the deceased was aged 55 years.
Her income is taken as Rs.18,35,436/- per annum.

20. As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect for the permanent employee has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 50%, 40 years to 50 years 30% and 50 to 60 years 15%.
In this case the deceased being an employee of the Central Government had a permanent job.
Therefore as per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 15% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.21,10,751/-(18,35,436 + 2,75,315).
21. It is compute that the petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased and of the petitioner No.1.
There are no any documents produced before the court to prove that the petitioner No.2 has got employment on compassionate ground in the said department, as such she is dependent of deceased.
22. The deceased died leaving behind 2 dependents.
As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd is to be deducted towards her personal expenses.
1/3rd of Rs.21,10,751/- works out to Rs.7,03,583/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.14,07,168/- p.a. ( 21,10,751 - 7,03,583).
Appropriate multiplier is '11'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.1,54,78,848/- (14,07,168 X 11).

Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.1,54,78,848/-
under the head of loss of dependency.

23. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

sentences.text: The PW.1 contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.

sentences.text: In this case, the petitioner No.1 is the husband, petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.

As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a mother cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their mother.

Therefore, petitioner 2 is entitled for Rs.44,000/-
under the head of Filial consortium.

 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.
Towards loss of dependency Rs.1,54,78,848/-
2. Towards loss of Consortium Rs.44,000/- to the petitioner No.1 3.

dead body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses 5.

consortium to petitioner and respondents No.2

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,55,99,848/-.
26.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the petitioner is the husband and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:50 respectively.
27. The petitioners are claiming interest @ 9% per annum on the compensation amount.
The respondent has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

28. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-F-0932.
It is not in dispute that respondent is not the owner of the offending vehicle.

29. Issue No.5:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,55,99,848/-(Rupees One Crore fifty five lakhs ninety nine thousand eight hundred and forty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 50%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 50% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

2) Whether the petitioners prove that on 04.06.2023 at about 3.05 to 3.10 p.m., when the deceased was proceeding as pillion rider in a scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-KD-4476 on Sheshadri Road, near Anandrao Flyover down ramp,
Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-40-F-0932 came from behind right side at very high speed and dashed against the scooter in which deceased was proceeding, due to which she succumbed to the injuries?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?
If so, to what extent and from whom ?
4) Whether the respondent proves that the petition is bad for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary parties?
5) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P10 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence of the bus.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Even in the instant case though the driver of the bus is examined as RW.1 to show that there was no negligence on his part, even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.
15. The petitioners with the help of Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P10 clearly demonstrated that there was negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-F-0932 by its driver.
In view of discussion made supra, the negligence is attributed on the driver of the bus and hence question of joinder of owner and insurer of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KD-4476 as necessary parties does not arise at all.
In this case, the petitioner No.1 is the husband, petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a mother cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their mother.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the petitioner is the husband and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

It is not in dispute that respondent is not the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, it is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
29. Issue No.5:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,55,99,848/-(Rupees One Crore fifty five lakhs ninety nine thousand eight hundred and forty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 50%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 and 2 a sum equal to 50% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 2 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
